chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. `Amrus al-Hamadani narrated to us in Hamadan. He said: Abu Ali al-Hasan b. Isma`il al-Qahtabi narrated to us. He said: Sa`id b. al-Hakam b. Abi Maryam narrated to us from his father from al-Awza`i from Yahya b. Abi Kathir from `Abdullah b. Murra from Salama b. Qays. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Ali is to the seventh heaven as the Sun is to the Earth during the day, and to the lowest heaven as the Moon is to the Earth during the night. Allah gave Ali so much virtue that if it were divided among the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them. And He gave him so much understanding that if it were divided among the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them.

His gentleness was likened to the gentleness of Lut, and his character to the character of Yahya, and his asceticism to the asceticism of Ayyub, and his generosity to the generosity of Ibrahim, and his splendour to the splendour of Sulayman b. Dawud, and his strength to the strength of Dawud.

His name is written upon every barrier in Paradise. My Lord gave me glad tidings of him, and it was good news to me. Ali is praiseworthy with the Truth, purified with the angels. He is my elite one, my sincere one, my manifest one, and my lantern, and my shield, and my companion. My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, made him amiable to me, so I asked my Lord not to take his soul before me, and I asked that He take his soul as a martyr. I was admitted into Paradise, and I saw that the houris of Ali were more than the leaves on the trees, and the palaces of Ali were as the number of humans.

Ali is from me, and I am from Ali. Whoever befriends Ali has befriended me. The love of Ali is a blessing, and following him is a virtue. The angels are brought near through him, and the righteous jinn surround him. No one walks the Earth after me except that he is more noble than him in honour, pride, and creed. He was never hasty, nor inclined to corruption, nor obstinate. The Earth carried him and it honoured him. No one came out of a womb after me more honourably than him. And he did not descend upon a place except that it was auspicious.

Allah bestowed wisdom upon him and clothed him with understanding. The angels sit with him but he does not see them. If revelation were to come to anyone after me, it would have come to him. So Allah adorned the gatherings by him, and ennobled the fortifications by him, and made the countries fertile by him, and gave the soldiers glory by him. His example is like that of the Sacred House of Allah: he is visited and he does not visit others. His example is like that of the Moon: when it rises, it illuminates the darkness. His example is like that of the Sun: when it rises, it illuminates the world. Allah described him in His Book and commended him with His verses, and described his effects in it, and maintained his stations. So he is the noble one when alive and the martyr when dead.
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the virtues and station of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition from al-Amali al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (s) delivers an extraordinary eulogy of Ali ibn Abi Talib, comparing him to celestial bodies and past prophets. The Prophet describes Ali's virtue and understanding as sufficient for all of Earth's inhabitants, likens his qualities to six prophets, and declares him worthy of revelation had it continued. Narrated through Salama b. Qays, this hadith was transmitted in the scholarly milieu of 4th-century Hamadan and represents one of the most comprehensive fadail (virtues) narrations about Ali in Shia literature.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. `Amr al-Hamadani narrated to us in Hamadan. He said: Abu `Ali al-Hasan b. Isma`il al-Qahtani narrated to us. He said: Sa`id b. al-Hakam b. Abi Maryam narrated to us from his father from al-Awza`i from Yahya b. Abi Kathir from `Abdullah b. Marra from Salama b. Qays.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: `Ali is to the seventh heaven as the Sun is to the Earth during the day and as the Moon is to the Earth during the night. Allah gave `Ali so much virtue that if He had allotted it to the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them. He gave him so much understanding that if He had allotted it to the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them.

His gentleness is like that of Lut, and his form is like that of Yahya, and his asceticism is like that of Ayyub, and his generosity is like that of Ibrahim, and his joy is like that of Sulayman b. Dawud, and his strength is like that of Dawud.

His name is written on every barrier in Paradise. My Lord gave me glad tidings of him, and it was good news to me. `Ali is considered praiseworthy by the truth, and he is considered purified by the angels. He is my elite one, my sincere one, my apparent one, my lantern, my garden, and my friend. My Lord made him amiable to me, so I asked my Lord to not cause him to die before me. I asked Him to cause him to die as a martyr. I entered Paradise, and I saw that `Ali had more houris than the leaves on a tree; and the palaces of `Ali are the number of humans [on Earth].

`Ali is from me, and I am from `Ali. Whoever befriends `Ali has befriended me. The love of `Ali is a blessing and following him is a virtue. The angels are brought near through him, and the righteous jinn walk due to him. No one will walk the Earth after me except that he is better than him in nobility, dignity, and creed. He is never hasty, nor corrupt, nor obstinate. The Earth carried him, yet he gave it honour. No one will come out of a womb after me in a way that is more honourable than his. He will not go to a place except that he would be auspicious.

Allah has bestowed wisdom upon him, and He has given him understanding. The angels attend to him, but he does not see them. If revelation were to come to anyone after me, it would have come to him. Allah has ornamented the gatherings by him, and He has ennobled the fortifications by him, and He made the countries fertile by him, and He has given the soldiers glory by him. His example is like that of the Sanctified House of Allah: he is visited, and he does not visit others. His example is like that of the Moon: when he rises, he illuminates the darkness. His example is like that of the Sun: when he rises, he illuminates the world. Allah has described him in His Book, and He has commended him in His verses, and He has described his effects in it, and He maintained his residences. He is noble when alive, and a martyr when dead.
